minutes.headline: Planning Board approved a common-driveway special permit and two stormwater permits, and cut three seats from the stalled Master Plan committee.
minutes.summary: The board endorsed an ANR, approved waivers and permits for 558/560 Goodridge Street and a stormwater permit for 255 Sunny Hill Road, continued 494 Electric Avenue to February 10, and signed written decisions. It heard the land use director's update on the state-mandated ADU and floodplain bylaw changes, including a dispute over a request to submit warrant motions by the end of the week. It restructured the Master Plan Steering Committee and agreed to wait for open space and agricultural input on 100 Townsend Harbor Road.

public_comment.topic: Advocated that 100 Townsend Harbor Road be taken by the town for Agricultural Commission community gardens, citing farmland history, town road access and municipal water.

Apologized for Zoom feedback, raised concern about Zoom host irregularities possibly being a hack, and said boards such as the Agricultural Commission are not being notified of applications needing vetting.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to approve a common-driveway special permit and a stormwater permit for 558 and 560 Goodridge Street, both with standard conditions.
The board voted 5-0 to remove the Finance Committee, Parks Commission and at-large seats from the Master Plan Steering Committee.
The board approved a stormwater permit for 255 Sunny Hill Road, conditioned on the town's engineering consultant being satisfied with the responses.
Members did not resolve a dispute over a request to submit warrant motions on the ADU bylaw by the end of the week; feedback goes to the land use director within a week.
The board continued the 494 Electric Avenue hearing to February 10 and will wait for other boards' input before taking a position on 100 Townsend Harbor Road.

why_it_matters: The ADU and floodplain bylaw changes are state-mandated and are headed for a town meeting warrant, so the timing dispute bears on how much review residents' boards get before a vote they may be asked to take.
The Master Plan Steering Committee now has no seat for the Finance Committee or Parks Commission, which changes whose input shapes a plan that guides later budget and land-use decisions.
